question: How does the SI define a metre? Give the speed-of-light value.

message.content:
The International System of Units (SI) defines the **metre** as:

> *The metre is the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1/299,792,458 of a second.*

This definition, adopted in 1983, fixes the speed of light in vacuum as an exact value:

> **Speed of light in vacuum, c = 299,792,458 metres per second (m/s)**

This means the metre is now defined in terms of a fundamental constant (the speed of light), ensuring high precision and reproducibility.
